title: Physical All-Predicate Multi-Cut Benchmark (Symmetric Threat Model)
motivation: The E22 theoretical audit (08_revision_v15/audits/e22_threat_model_breadth_sensitivity.json) established, via the deterministic planner alone, that when the attacker may invalidate either member of each F5 pair (A/B, C/D, E/F) rather than the fixed A/C/E of E21's restricted threat model, the minimum certificate becomes all six predicates and DCJI predicts no strict reduction over FullRefresh. This experiment re-derives that result physically: six independent Kubernetes ConfigMaps (as in E21), a symmetric-threat scenario (F5_PHYS_SYM) whose transitions allow any of the six predicates to be individually cut, and live trials across all 8 minimal invalidating cuts plus a stable control, measuring real physical request counts and latency for both guards.
notes: Preregistered post-hoc extension (E25), run outside the locked v8.1.1 package and outside all other v9/E21/E22/E23/E24 evidence. Uses a dedicated namespace/ConfigMaps, not E21's. This experiment's expected/confirmatory finding is a NULL result for cost reduction (DCJI == FullRefresh == 6 queries in every condition), which is itself the physical confirmation of E22's theoretical claim -- a null result here is the predicted, correct outcome, not a failure of the experiment.
